Now I want to visually verify the dimension labels match the right segments and check for other issues like door swings. The title block date and scale (1:100, confirmed against the 10.00m/283.46pt measurement) look consistent, so next I'll check the door swings.

Looking at the door between WOHNEN and SCHLAFEN, I'm tracing the arc and opening geometry to confirm the hinge position and swing direction make sense relative to the wall opening — the hinge appears to sit at one end of the 1.00m opening with the leaf sweeping from a horizontal closed position into the room.

Actually the opening spans south of the hinge, so the swing arc seems to be on the wrong side of the opening — possibly a generator quirk rather than a real error. I should check the other doors to see if this pattern holds consistently, starting with the second door in the horizontal wall, examining its gap coordinates and arc geometry.

For that door, the closed leaf position lines up correctly with the opening and swings north into SCHLAFEN, which looks consistent. Now I'm checking the entrance door's gap and arc coordinates in the bottom wall to verify its geometry too.

Turning back to door 1, I'm examining the opening rectangle and hinge position to see whether the leaf lines align properly with the wall face.

This could be an intentional seeded error, so I want to zoom in and visually confirm the swing arc placement. I also note the mixed units (cm for wall thickness like 30 and 11.5, meters elsewhere) are conventional in Austrian/German plans, so that's not an issue.

Looking more closely at the SCHLAFEN door, I can see the white gap in the wall sits just below the arc's hinge line, around y_img 535-590, with the leaf sweeping upward from there.

Comparing this to the BAD door, where the gap and arc span exactly the same x-range, confirms the mismatch — the WOHNEN→SCHLAFEN door's swing arc is offset from its wall opening by the full door width of 1.00 m, drawn above rather than aligned with the opening. I'm now wondering whether this offset is an intentional error or just an artifact.

Checking the arc radii against opening widths, all three doors have radii matching their opening sizes correctly — so the sizing is fine, only the positioning of door 1 is off. I'm flagging this as a lower-confidence finding given the uncertainty about intent.

Now I'm compiling the main quantitative errors: the 5.86 dimension is actually drawn as 5.80 m, the 4.00 dimension is drawn as roughly 3.49 m, and the dimension chain doesn't sum correctly (0.30+5.86+0.115+4.00+0.30 = 10.575, not the labeled 10.00 m). I'm also noting the WOHNEN area label of 31.2 m² is wrong — the actual area computes to 37.1 m² (5.80 × 6.40) — and starting to check the SCHLAFEN area label next.

I'm now verifying SCHLAFEN's labeled 13.4 m² against the actual computed area of 14.2 m² (3.49 × 4.09), and BAD's labeled 6.9 m² against its actual 7.7 m² (3.49 × 2.20). Three area errors feels like a lot, so I'm trying to sanity-check whether these areas were derived from some alternate set of dimensions — testing ratios like 13.4/3.485 and 13.4/4.085 to see if a consistent height value explains the discrepancy, and checking whether the shortfalls for SCHLAFEN (94.1%) and BAD (90.0%) follow any systematic pattern. They don't match cleanly, so I'm considering other explanations for where these area figures came from.

None of the labeled areas match my computed values, which seems odd since a generator would typically leave most correct. I'm trying a different approach now, reconsidering whether the wall between SCHLAFEN and BAD is placed differently, and working backward from an assumed right block width to see if that reconciles the numbers.

Trying the 5.86/4.00 label widths instead: WOHNEN gives h=5.324, SCHLAFEN h1=3.35, BAD h2=1.725, but h1+h2+0.115=5.19 doesn't match 5.324 — still inconsistent. I wonder if this is a synthetic drawing with independent random errors in the area labels rather than a real consistent floor plan, so I should just report the measured vs. labeled discrepancies rather than force a fit. Let me double-check the scale isn't the source of error before concluding that.

Checking the remaining segments confirms the "11.5" and "30" labels match their tick positions correctly. The 5.80 vs 5.86 discrepancy looks like a clear transposed-digit error, but the 3.485 vs 4.00 gap is much larger at 51.5 cm, so I'm wondering if there's a different explanation for that one.

Testing whether the drawn pair (5.80+3.485=9.285) or the labeled pair (5.86+4.00=9.80) matches the required interior total of 9.285 cm, I find the drawn geometry is self-consistent while both labels are wrong — so I can't tell if a wall was misplaced or just mislabeled, but I'll flag both label mismatches plus the chain-sum discrepancy. Now I'm rechecking the area labels against computed values, starting with WOHNEN at 37.12 m² versus its label of 31.2.

Checking SCHLAFEN (14.24 vs 13.4) and BAD (7.67 vs 6.9), all three areas differ from their labels, suggesting they were computed from entirely different geometry. I try backing out implied heights from the labeled areas and dimensions, but the numbers don't reconcile (5.075+0.115=5.19 vs WOHNEN's implied 5.324), so I'm now testing whether a drawn height of 6.40 produces consistent results instead.

Maybe the areas exclude wall finishes or represent usable floor space rather than gross area, though that seems unlikely too. I should check if there's a second page, examine the layers, and look for any hidden or overlapping text like stacked labels.
